chunks: And it is narrated from Masʿadah ibn Ṣadaqah that he said:

Abū ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام was asked: Why is it that you do not call the fornicator a disbeliever, while you call the one who abandons salat (prayer) a disbeliever? And what is the proof regarding that?

So he said: Because the fornicator and those similar to him only do that because of desire, since it overcomes him. But the one who abandons salat (prayer) does not abandon it except out of belittlement toward it. That is because you do not find the fornicator approaching a woman except while taking pleasure in coming to her and intending her. And everyone who abandons salat (prayer), intending to abandon it, his purpose in abandoning it is not pleasure. So when pleasure is absent, belittlement occurs; and when belittlement occurs, kufr occurs.

key_terms.اسْتِخْفَافًا: belittlement, disdain, or treating something lightly
key_terms.الزَّانِيَ: the fornicator; one who commits zina
key_terms.الشَّهْوَةِ: desire or lust that drives the act
key_terms.الْحُجَّةُ: the proof or reasoning for a judgment
key_terms.الْكُفْرُ: disbelief; here, the state resulting from disdain toward the obligation

ai.seo_question: Why is a fornicator not called a disbeliever while one who abandons prayer is called a disbeliever in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith distinguishes between a sin committed under the force of desire and the deliberate abandonment of salat (prayer) out of disdain. It presents ترک الصلاة as an act indicating istikhfaf, or belittlement of a divine obligation, which is why it is described here in terms of kufr.
